problem: Object-goal navigation methods that learn on pixel-level semantic maps or use only object-level relations suffer from 'geometric myopia' and low exploration efficiency because they lack high-level room-level structure modeling in complex indoor scenes.
motivation: Room-level functional attributes and topology give strong priors on where target objects are likely to be (e.g., bed in bedroom), which could guide long-range exploration of unobserved regions. The paper builds explicit room-level graph reasoning and fuses it with geometric constraints.
key_idea: Build an online room-level topological semantic graph, reason over unobserved regions with a GAT to produce semantic heatmaps, and fuse them with geometric hard constraints via a Product-of-Experts inside a PPO goal-selection policy.
insight: Explicit room-level semantic reasoning gives gains especially for objects with strong spatial correlation to room type (bed 73.2%, toilet 72.5% SR, over 20% gain over baselines). Only the abstract is available, so ablation details are not known.
method: Online room segmentation: converts unstructured sensory data/local observations into a room-level topological graph with functional attributes and connectivity
GAT semantic reasoning: Graph Attention Network infers semantic attributes of unobserved regions, giving priors for long-range exploration
Product of Experts fusion: combines semantic reasoning heatmaps with geometric hard constraints (reachability)
PPO goal-selection policy: selects long-term navigation goals with semantic consistency and physical reachability

setting.backbone: GAT + PPO policy (details not given in abstract)
setting.training_data: Gibson dataset in Habitat (details not given in abstract)
setting.observation: egocentric sensory data building semantic map (RGB-D likely; not specified in abstract)
setting.action_space: long-term goal selection on map (global policy) with low-level planner

numbers.evidence: Abstract: 'SPL of 0.340 ... total success rate of 68.4%'

numbers_note: abstract only; split is not specified in the abstract (reported as 'val' as a placeholder); per-object SRs: bed 73.2, toilet 72.5.
results: SSAG reaches SPL 0.340 and SR 68.4% on Habitat/Gibson, outperforming SemExp by 15.3% and SemGO by 4.9% in SPL. Bed and toilet SR reach 73.2% and 72.5%, over 20% gain vs baselines.
limitations: Only evaluated in simulation (Habitat/Gibson); no real-robot validation stated
Relies on online room segmentation quality, which may fail in ambiguous layouts
